answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped unless it posts a bond that is forfeited when independent auditors prove coordinated identities are controlled by one party. Auditors compare signed interaction histories and shared funding paths, then submit evidence to a challenge process; the bond pays for review and rewards challengers. A sybil operator must therefore lock capital across accounts and risk losing it, rather than gain influence by cheaply minting identities. A plume of linked accounts may look like a comet crossing an ocean, but shared control leaves costly traces.
